Subject: Leadership comms playbook + QBR OKRs checkpoint

Team —

I drafted a lightweight 'leadership comms playbook' and an OKR checkpoint checklist for the upcoming QBR. The goal is to give people a short template (30–45 minute sync + follow-up cadence) they can use for any squad-level change or role adjustment so messaging is consistent and reduces rework from PR reviews.

High-level:
- A 3-part sender script (context, impact, ask) for execs/managers
- FAQ fragment to pre-populate for common questions (jobs, timelines, support)
- A small OKR check list for QBRs to call out regressions, mitigations, and owner commitments

I attached v1 of the playbook and the OKR checklist. Would like:
1) Jonas — signal any missing risks or escalation wording we must include for Dedicated/Private customers.
2) Marissa — please sanity-check the timeline and whether Legal needs to pre-review the external-facing language.
3) Mina — can you add a short ops runbook blurb for rollback/fallback?

Target: finalize by EOD Wednesday so we can circulate to leads before QBR dry-runs Thursday.

Thanks —
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategy & Ops, Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0123 | tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Leadership comms playbook + QBR OKRs checkpoint

Tessa —

Thanks for the draft; good structure. A couple quick notes after a skim:
- Under 'impact' section, add an explicit bullet for SLA/latency expectations when we mention Dedicated capacity moves — customers will escalate if we don't call out SLOs.
- Add a short paragraph on data residency/litigation holds for Private deployments (one-liner we can paste into FAQs).
- For escalation wording: remove 'immediate' and replace with 'within 24–48 hours' unless it's a Sev1; Legal prefers that vagueness to avoid promises we can't guarantee.

I'll ping infra to confirm the rollback bullet you asked Mina to author; I think we can standardize a two-step fallback (model variant switch, then scale-up) in the runbook.

Small wording suggestion inside the checklist: separate 'regression' vs 'performance deviation' so we don't conflate functional correctness with latency/cost changes.

If you want, I can inline edits directly into the doc and send back.

—Jonas
